questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Arctic Nature and small town with unique experiences. The courses also promised lots of fieldwork.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I studied at UNIS - The University Centre in Svalbard. Not UiO.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everything was in the appropriate emails, and I always knew where to go.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None. It was easy

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Samskipnaden Elvesletta is the only place with student housing, and it's pretty great.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You're technically loving off campus, but it takes 5 min to walk to UNIS, so it never feels like it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: To go to UNIS, you need to apply individually outside of the Erasmus exchange with UiO. When accepted, UiO and KU is informed. Both UNIS and UiO will send you mails, and most of the UiO can be ignored. All further sign-up information can be found in the e-mails and is really easy to follow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always write to UNIS and most likely have an answer by the end of the day. It is a very small institution.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: You get accepted directly to specific classes, when accepted to UNIS. So you are guaranteed a spot.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go for it. They try to make the classes 50% Norwegian and 50% other and the places are given based on grades, but sometimes there's not enough Norwegian students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Overall it was a bit easier than at KU, mostly because of the lack of math. The exams I took were oral, and were almost impossible to fail.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Most of the lectures were given by external lecturers travelling to Longyearbyen for a week or so. They were all prominent researchers within the stuff they taught, so it was quite nice. 
It was a bit confusing with the litterature, since we mostly got compendiums and PowerPoint slides and we did not have a specific book.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
AGF213 - Polar Meteorology and Climate (15 ECTS)
AGF214 - Polar Ocean Climate (15 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: These courses were great. There are not that many to choose from, but from what I've heard they're all interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
There were a lot of cold-climate and hiking gear I did not have from home. I think I spend 10.000 DKK on boots, jackets, pants, spikes, woollen basde layers, head lamps, gloves, riffel license etc. 
It could probably be done cheaper, but I bought from durable brands and new. But if you have previous experience with cold weather and proper layering, you probably have most of this stuff already.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were really expensive, but it was expected. On the other hand there was no transport cost, because the city is literally only 2 km wide. If you're staying in the spring semester, there might be an extra cost when it comes to renting/buying a snowscooter.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is a very nice sports opportunities in Longyearbyen with a sports hall, climbing wall, swimmingpool, football field, ice-skating, dancing, run-club, shooting club and I could go on. 
And then of course so much hiking!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go hiking. See the ice-caves and the sunset from the mountain tops. Eat lunch with the reindeer. Just get out of the house:)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get some sports going, hike, get to know some locals and you might find yourself on a free sled-dog ride:)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Norwegian is themain language, but everyone speaks english.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was just very intercultural, so occasionally things got lost in translation, but nothing severe.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The small-town feeling, where everyone came to the northern-most Blues Festival, and where everyone shows up in support for the big-band.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Many layers when it comes to clothing
2. Facillitate connections both among people from you course and your kitchen, as well as students who've been here for a long time. Then you get all the tips and tricks, and might be able to buy their old flare gun. 
3. Vitamin D pills, or the polar night will strangle you in the darkness.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Show up early to friday gathering. It's not as fun if everyone shows up late.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people and the nature. Everyone is kind, and I can honestly say I've never been to a more beautiful place.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The polar night. 24h darkness is not that fun after a while.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
